title: the verdict runs its instruments a few at a time
intention: The verdict gate runs a ticket's instruments a few at a time instead of one after another, so a big ticket's verdict, and every ticket queued behind it, finishes in a fraction of the time.
why: Measured 2026-11-16: 149b9a1ab9c4's verdict ran its 74 instruments one after another in observe_instruments, 1470 s of runs (median 15 s, max 221 s), 1500 s from ask to berth. 62a8ecb673a7's verdict waited 562 s behind it in the one verdict FIFO. This fixes 149b-class verdicts. It does not fix the worst case at the declared timeouts, 74 x 600 s = 44,400 s, which width 3 only divides and which stays past the asker's 3600 s berth wait (a bound, not a measurement). A verdict-wide bound is its own ticket and is not cast here.
traces_to: Law 1: the resolver and the box are spent on the novel. One big verdict serially blocks every other ticket's verdict.
how: In observe_instruments, after every command is extracted (0d38d0f5a4e3), run the planned runs on concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=VERDICT_WIDTH), VERDICT_WIDTH = 3 a module constant, and return the readings in planned order. Admission is by memory: a run starts only while MemAvailable is at least 2 x SEAL_SWAP_BYTES + a 1 GB floor, read from /proc/meminfo through an injectable reader; otherwise it waits for a running slot to free. Each observed run carries started and ended epochs. Before PROVEME the build samples MemAvailable, Shmem and df /tmp every 5 s through one real 149b verdict and records them in measured. A red at width 3 is recorded as it came; child b7068b1ba431 re-runs it alone and carries Q#119's hypothesis and its WATCHME (outline 9.4.8.1.1, 0.6.1). BUILDME waits on 6ea3a8548493, which moves the one live write among these proofs to scratch.

measured.saw: 149b's verdict: 74 observed_runs, all pass, seconds summing 1470 (min 8.0, median 15.3, max 220.7); asked 02:38:08 MST, berthed 03:03:08
62a8's verdict asked 02:53:46, ran 03:03:08 to 03:05:31 (143 s, 1 instrument plus dispose), so it waited 562 s in the FIFO behind 149b
a smaller cost, not fixed here: StageGate._dispose re-runs the hypothesis instruments (2 of 149b's 74) that the door then runs again
measured.how: comparing the hypothesize berth's instruments with the validate criteria for 149b

measured.saw: sealed runs are isolated only at ~/.cairn: each binds its own /tmp/cairn-instance-seal-<pid> swap over ~/.cairn under bwrap --dev-bind / /, and builds its own pristine copy, each ~596 MB on tmpfs /tmp (7.7 GB, 2.9 GB used). The repo, /tmp, the network and git are shared between concurrent runs; the network seal is retired
measured.how: reading cairn/devices/tester/isolation.py:459 and :757, and du of a live swap and pristine on akiendelllinux

measured.saw: of 274 write sites in 149b's 74 proofs, 273 are scratch; one writes the live tickets store (test_transitions' demo teeth), which a concurrent test_v2_migration glob-then-read can race. Ticket 6ea3a8548493 moves it to scratch
measured.how: an AST classifier over the 74 proofs' write calls, unresolved sites read by hand

measured.saw: MemAvailable 6.19 GB with 12 scratch buses running, 6.38 GB after stopping them

outcomes.claim: with an injected runner sleeping 0.4 s per run, 9 runnable instruments return from observe_instruments in under 2 s (serial is 3.6 s)
the readings come back in the artifact's verdicts order, each carrying the run of its own command
never more than VERDICT_WIDTH runs are in flight at once, counted by the injected runner
an artifact with one unrunnable instrument still returns every reading with runnable False or True and zero runs made
with an injected meminfo reader below 2 x SEAL_SWAP_BYTES + 1 GB, no further run starts while one is in flight, and runs resume when the reader rises; the first run always starts
every observed run carries started and ended epochs, ended >= started, and with width 3 at least two runs' intervals overlap

constraints: observe_instruments runs its planned runs on a bounded pool of VERDICT_WIDTH (3) and keeps planned order.

admission by memory in verdict.py: up to VERDICT_WIDTH, a run starts only while MemAvailable >= 2 x SEAL_SWAP_BYTES + 1 GB (SEAL_SWAP_BYTES = the measured ~596 MB swap); the meminfo reader is injectable. The first run is always admitted, so a tight box degrades to serial, never to zero.
each observed run records started and ended epochs beside seconds.
a red-first proof drives observe_instruments with an injected sleeping, counting runner and an injected meminfo reader over a scratch artifact, one tooth per clause.
